text: One day a new group of prisoners arrived, and among them was a tall, strong man of sixty with a short gray beard. <break time="0.8s" /> He said he had been arrested only for taking a horse, but added that he had once done something truly wrong and never been caught. <break time="0.8s" /> He said that he came from Vladimir and that his name was Makar Semyonich, and Aksionov, raising his head, asked about the Aksionov family. <break time="0.8s" /> Makar answered that they were rich, though their father was in Siberia, and then the others told him how Aksionov had been wrongly punished. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing this, Makar slapped his knee and cried, Well, this is wonderful, But how old you have grown, Grandfather. <break time="0.8s" /> When Aksionov asked whether he knew who had killed the merchant, Makar said, It must have been the man in whose bag the knife was found. <break time="0.8s" /> How could anyone put a knife into your bag while it was under your head, It would surely have woken you up. <break time="0.8s" /> Hearing these words, Aksionov felt sure that this was the man who had killed the merchant, and he got up and went away. <break time="0.8s" /> All that night he lay awake, remembering his young wife and children, and so great was his anger against Makar that he longed for revenge.
